ENDOMETRIUM. Progestogens are used in the treatment of ad- vanced endometrial carcinoma (p.663) but there are doubts about their value in the earlier stages of disease.1 Medroxy- progesterone acetate was effective in a rare case of low-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma.2 It has also been used in a few patients as adjuvant therapy after surgery3 and for the treat- ment of metastatic disease.4 1. Respiratory disorders. Reviews of the use of medroxypro- gesterone acetate in obstructive sleep apnoea have concluded that it has a limited role.1,2 Progesterone and, more commonly, medroxyprogesterone ace- tate are used in the treatment of pulmonary lymphangioleiomyo- matosis, a rare disease affecting only women.3-7 Anecdotal evi- dence suggests some patients improve or stabilise on treatment, possibly those with chylous effusions or chylous ascites.8 How- ever, a more rapid decline in lung function has also been ob- served with progestogen therapy in some groups.5,6 Medroxyprogesterone acetate was reported to be effective in treating congenital
